summary: The spread-statistics block is internally consistent, and the non-target script correctly subtracts additive counts from the full and target tables. However, that subtraction cannot answer the stated policy question of whether replacing names on all records performs worse than replacing names only on targets; the completed target-only linkage run must be scored directly against the all-new run. The derived recall figures also report more precision than the rounded source rates support.

findings.title: The non-target subtraction does not compare all-record replacement with target-only replacement
findings.what_the_code_does: The script subtracts each target-table statistic from the corresponding all-record statistic and then compares the paper's globally run `Old` and `New` linkages. It never reads or scores the target-only linkage files. Moreover, ABE invokes `abematch ... unique_m(2) unique_f(2)` and retains links using `unique_file2 == 1 & unique_match2 == 1`, so changing target records can alter the candidate uniqueness of non-target records.
findings.why_it_matters: The resulting decline for non-target records cannot be attributed specifically to replacing their names. It may also include linkage spillovers caused by changing target names. Therefore these figures do not establish the brief's stated objective—whether replacing names on all records hurt relative to replacing names only on targets—and could support the wrong implementation choice.
findings.how_to_check: After `_tgt_only_run.do` finishes, score `link1930_1940_mltgt1940_cleaned_noraceblock0.dta` and `link1930_1940_ml1940_cleaned_noraceblock0.dta` on the identical non-target histids. Tabulate links retained, partners changed, and Verified/Unverifiable/Contradicted categories directly between those two runs; do the analogous target-only run for HLINK if the conclusion covers HLINK.
findings.suggested_fix: Use the target-only and all-new linkage outputs as the actual comparison. Retain this All-minus-Target calculation only as a descriptive Old-versus-New result for non-target records, and label it explicitly as unable to isolate the effect of replacing non-target names.

findings.title: Non-target recall is printed to two decimals although it is reconstructed from rounded rates
findings.what_the_code_does: The code reconstructs two true-link denominators as `V / (printed recall / 100)`, subtracts them, and prints `100*V/den` with `%5.2f`. Each input recall is already rounded to two decimal percentage points, and differencing the reconstructed denominators propagates that uncertainty nonlinearly.
findings.why_it_matters: The last reported digits are not identified by the source tables. For example, allowing each printed recall to differ from its underlying value by 0.005 percentage points places ABE-exact Old non-target recall at approximately 38.571%–38.599%, spanning several distinct two-decimal outputs rather than uniquely supporting 38.58%.
findings.how_to_check: For each source recall `r`, recompute the result at all four combinations where the full- and target-sample rates equal `r-0.005` or `r+0.005`. Compare the minimum and maximum with the value printed by line 63.
findings.suggested_fix: Prefer the exact true-pair denominators from the linkage output. If only the tables are available, print recall to one decimal place or report an interval induced by the source rounding rather than a two-decimal point estimate.

verified_clean.item: Full-minus-target arithmetic is valid for the additive link-quality counts.
verified_clean.evidence: MATCHING/nontarget_from_tables.py:59-60 subtracts Verified, Unverifiable, and Directly Contradicted counts column by column, and lines 42-45 verify that each table's categories sum to its printed match rate under the stated denominator.

verified_clean.item: The table column mapping is correct.
verified_clean.evidence: MATCHING/nontarget_from_tables.py:49-52 maps Jaro-Winkler to columns 0/1 and ABE exact to columns 2/3, matching the source table headings; HLINK correctly uses columns 0/1.

verified_clean.item: The parser stops at the end of Panel A and checks that every required row was found.
verified_clean.evidence: MATCHING/nontarget_from_tables.py:28-39 breaks at the next `midrule` after collecting rows and asserts that Match Rate, Verified, Unverifiable, Directly Contradicted, and Recall are all present.

verified_clean.item: The new spread summaries use the requested samples and measures.
verified_clean.evidence: MATCHING/profile_names_jw.do:250-258 selects full-name JW for men and first-name JW for women, restricted to `has_dmonth & hasml`, with groups all, cell 0, and cells 1-4.

verified_clean.item: The spread block computes paired differences on identical nonmissing samples.
verified_clean.evidence: MATCHING/profile_names_jw.do:252 constructs `_d` record by record, while lines 258-267 summarize Ancestry, model, and `_d` under the same condition and assert equal `r(N)` values.

verified_clean.item: The standardized spread quantity is implemented and labelled consistently.
verified_clean.evidence: MATCHING/profile_names_jw.do:245-247 defines `diff/SD` as mean difference divided by Ancestry's JW standard deviation, and line 270 computes exactly `dm/as`.

verified_clean.item: The changed profile output describes similarity rather than ground-truth accuracy.
verified_clean.evidence: MATCHING/profile_names_jw.do:245-247 consistently calls the outcome Jaro-Winkler similarity and labels the groups by Ancestry–FamilySearch agreement.

verified_clean.item: The Python input path can be overridden rather than being unconditionally machine-specific.
verified_clean.evidence: MATCHING/nontarget_from_tables.py:15 and MATCHING/nontarget_from_tables.py:21 accept the paper repository as the first command-line argument, using the local D: path only as a default.

review_limits: No paper draft was supplied, so claims-vs-code could not be checked against manuscript language.
The external census microdata were unavailable and the Stata pipeline was not run; actual generated spread values and linkage results could not be independently reproduced.
The four generated TeX linkage tables were readable and the Python script ran successfully, but their upstream data construction was not rerun.
The target-only linkage job had not produced scored outputs, so the direct target-only-versus-all-new comparison could not be evaluated.
Review was scoped to the uncommitted working-tree changes and necessary local context, not the entire repository.
